distillation_scope: Pure disease-name leaf distillation for the full clinical spectrum of Lyme disease. Early localized, early disseminated, and late manifestations are represented as mechanisms, axes, stages, and context modifiers rather than as first-level disease ids.

latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Transmission of Borrelia burgdorferi sensu lato complex from an Ixodes tick after compatible outdoor or endemic-area exposure. This is an upstream exposure gate and not proof of active disease by itself.

Spirochete expansion in skin near the inoculation site with local innate and adaptive inflammation. This produces erythema migrans when clinically visible, but absence of recalled tick bite or rash does not exclude downstream Lyme disease.

Migration of Borrelia from skin to blood, nervous tissue, myocardium, joints, and other sites. Dissemination explains multiple erythema migrans lesions, cranial neuropathy, meningoradiculitis, carditis, and later arthritis.

Host inflammatory response to local or disseminated Borrelia infection causing fever, chills, headache, malaise, myalgia, arthralgia, and inflammatory-marker elevation. The response is often milder than pyogenic bacterial sepsis.

Inflammation in meninges, cranial nerves, nerve roots, or peripheral nerves causing lymphocytic meningitis, headache, meningismus, radicular pain, neuropathy, and CSF lymphocytic pleocytosis with elevated protein.
Inflammation of cranial nerves, most classically facial nerve palsy but also ocular motor palsies, causing facial weakness, diplopia, and other focal cranial neuropathies.

Inflammation of cardiac conduction tissue and myocardium producing fluctuating PR prolongation, second- or third-degree AV block, bradycardia, syncope, myocarditis physiology, and rarely circulatory collapse.

Inflammatory synovitis, typically mono- or oligoarticular and knee-predominant, with large effusion, high synovial WBC, pain, warmth, and swelling. It can occur months after infection and may mimic septic arthritis or prosthetic joint infection.

Persistent synovitis after microbiologic control, driven by retained antigens and host immune activation rather than by routine culture-positive pyogenic infection. This mechanism should not be interpreted as proof of persistent viable organism.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Late cutaneous or ocular inflammatory involvement
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Less common late or extracutaneous manifestations such as acrodermatitis chronica atrophicans, borrelial lymphocytoma, keratitis, uveitis, optic neuritis, or other ocular inflammation. These are spectrum axes, not separate first-level Lyme disease manifolds.

Fatigue, pain, or cognitive symptoms that can persist after appropriate treatment in a minority of patients. This is a symptom-persistence pathway and should not be used as a direct active-infection label.

mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Tick inoculation seeds local skin infection after an incubation interval.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: More likely when early infection is untreated or host response does not clear local infection.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Borrelia can disseminate from the inoculation site to nervous, cardiac, and articular tissues.
Local infection can produce fever, headache, chills, malaise, myalgia, and arthralgia.
Disseminated Borrelia can involve meninges, nerve roots, and peripheral nerves.
Cranial neuritis is a common neurologic expression of Lyme neuroborreliosis.
Cardiac tissue involvement usually occurs within weeks of infection and can produce AV block.
Late Lyme arthritis reflects articular involvement after prior dissemination.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: Most relevant when objective synovitis persists after appropriate antimicrobial therapy.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Persistent joint inflammation can remain after antimicrobial treatment.
Borrelia can produce less common ocular or late cutaneous inflammatory manifestations.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: Only after documented or clinically compatible Lyme disease and treatment; not a standalone active infection proof.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Some patients have prolonged fatigue, pain, or cognitive symptoms after acute illness.

mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Heart-rate direction depends on whether inflammatory fever or conduction block dominates.
Bradyarrhythmia can cause presyncope, syncope, or unresponsiveness.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: Often normal in isolated conduction disease; rises with myocarditis.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Troponin reflects myocardial injury when present.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: Elevates with myocardial stress or transient heart failure physiology.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: BNP/NT-proBNP can mark cardiac strain in Lyme carditis.
Objective arthritis is the core late joint manifestation.
Lyme arthritis often produces large-joint swelling.
Effusion is often clinically or radiographically evident.
Effusion and synovitis limit range of motion.
Inflammatory synovial fluid WBC can be high and mimic septic arthritis.
Synovial fluid may be neutrophil predominant despite Borrelia etiology.
Persistent synovitis after antibiotic therapy drives refractory arthritis hazard.
Borrelial lymphocytoma is a recognized but uncommon cutaneous manifestation.
Acrodermatitis chronica atrophicans is a late European-predominant manifestation.
Ocular inflammation can occur in a minority of cases.
Conduction-system inflammation can progress quickly to high-grade AV block.
High-grade AV block can cause syncope, severe bradycardia, or arrest.
Neuroborreliosis can cause persistent focal neurologic deficits.
Prolonged untreated synovitis can damage joint function.
Cardiac arrest is the principal short-term mortality path in Lyme disease.
Severe neurologic involvement can raise mortality indirectly, though death from Lyme neuroborreliosis is uncommon.

Pregnancy context often shifts selection toward beta-lactam options.
Tetracycline avoidance limits doxycycline feasibility.

side_effects.interpretation: GI intolerance can impair oral absorption.

treatments.context_specific_role: Active oral anti-Borrelia therapy for many early localized, early disseminated non-severe, and arthritis contexts when feasible.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Clinically significant beta-lactam allergy limits use.

treatments.context_specific_role: Alternative active oral anti-Borrelia beta-lactam path.

Severe cephalosporin allergy limits ceftriaxone.

Biliary sludging or cholestatic toxicity context.

treatments.context_specific_role: Symptom and effusion support in Lyme arthritis while antimicrobial or postinfectious management addresses the cause.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Immune-directed therapy is a post-antibiotic persistent-synovitis path, not an acute infection substitute.

treatments.context_specific_role: Post-antibiotic persistent synovitis path after active infection has been treated and pyogenic infection excluded.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Post-exposure prophylaxis only applies to high-risk recent tick-bite contexts.

treatments.context_specific_role: Prevention path after high-risk Ixodes bite before symptoms; not a treatment for established Lyme disease.

supportive_care: Do not use Lyme serology, CSF antibody index, or synovial fluid PCR as ordinary presentation evidence. Store them as confirmatory context with use_in_ranking:false in case JSON.
Preserve absence of recalled tick bite or rash when reported. Many true cases do not recall a bite, and absence of EM should not delete neurologic, cardiac, or arthritis evidence.
Record timing from exposure and symptom onset, because early localized, early disseminated, and late arthritis patterns are time dependent.
For suspected carditis, obtain ECG, telemetry, PR interval, AV block degree, symptoms of syncope/presyncope, troponin/BNP when available, and pacing context.
For neurologic presentations, structure headache, meningismus, cranial neuropathy, radicular pain, CSF WBC, lymphocyte fraction, protein, glucose, and neuroimaging results.
For arthritis, structure joint presence, swelling, effusion, warmth/erythema, range of motion, synovial WBC/differential/crystals/culture, ESR/CRP, and prosthetic joint context.
Evaluate Babesia, Anaplasma, Ehrlichia, rickettsial illness, viral meningitis, septic arthritis, and noninfectious mimics through their own axes or manifolds rather than by narrowing Lyme evidence.
Treatment ranking should emerge from organ involvement, route feasibility, pregnancy/allergy context, oral absorption, high-grade AV block hazard, neuroborreliosis axes, and arthritis persistence.
Post-treatment symptom persistence is represented as a symptom pathway, not as a hard-coded active infection label.
quality_notes: The disease-specific input used for this distillation is only the disease name: Lyme disease.
Exactly one derived_hazard axis is present: mortality_hazard_in_D-LYME-DISEASE.
Major complications are event_hazard axes with hazard_drift/event edges into outcome.
Treatment schema uses outcome-emergent ranking only; no hand-authored priority-label fields are present.
All treatment trajectory_modifications fields are dictionaries keyed by axis or mechanism id.
